name: Asphodel Green
lede: Asphodel Green is a muted, yellowish green named for a flower of Greek legend.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines asphodel as the rich yellow of the daffodil, and asphodel green as a yellowish green [1]. The color is in the library from three sources: Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* (plate XLI), ISCC-NBS block 120, and Maerz and Paul, which first recorded it in 1912 [2].

Maerz and Paul also list a near neighbor, Nile, first recorded in 1888 [2]. The nearest standard color is [[moss]], at a distance of 4.0 [2]. It sits among the greens near [[olive]] and [[celadon]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, the color appears in 1.07% of them, as photographed [3]. It is more common than 63% of the named colors and peaks in the 1900s, at 2.9 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 36% of cases [3]. Harald Giersing is its most devoted painter here, with 4 of 23 works [3].
